title: Max Leads the Earth Day Cleanup
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for the McKinley Bulldogs.

pages: For Earth Day, the fifth graders at McKinley are in charge of a schoolwide cleanup. Each fifth grader is paired with a younger buddy class. Max's buddies are a group of first graders, and they are very excited to wear the big plastic gloves. "Rule number one," Max tells them, "never touch anything sharp or gross. Point to it, and a grown-up will handle it."

The team starts in the South Yard. They find candy wrappers stuck in the fence, a lost mitten, bottle caps, and about a million tiny pieces of plastic. One first grader holds up a stick. "Is this trash?" Max laughs. "No, that is nature. Nature stays."

Back at the bins, Max teaches everyone how to sort. Food scraps and paper napkins go in the green compost bin. Clean bottles, cans, and paper go in the blue recycling bin. Things that cannot be recycled or composted, like chip bags, go in the landfill bin. "Why does it matter?" asks a buddy. Max explains that compost turns into soil for gardens, recycling becomes new things, and landfill trash stays in the ground for a very, very long time.

Max's class also collects data. They count every piece of trash and make a tally chart. When they add it up, they have collected 312 pieces, and 147 of them were plastic. "That's almost half!" says Kai. The class decides to make posters for the MPR reminding everyone to use reusable water bottles and lunch containers.

At the end of the day, the yard looks sparkling clean. Max's buddies give Max a giant thank-you card covered in drawings of the Earth wearing a smile. Max tapes it inside a locker. Taking care of the planet is a big job, Max thinks, but it starts with one wrapper, one bin, and one school.
